OPEN-SIDED FLANK FORGE WITH THE LAMP-EYED OWL: a forge hall high on the volcano's shoulder open through three wide arches of unequal span to the bright air beyond, one great arched furnace set into the inner mountain wall at the far end breathing orange, heavy timber gantries crossing overhead at uneven heights, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre beneath the narrowest arch, a stone owl perched on the nearest gantry beam with two round eyes lit amber from within like lamps

SUNKEN FORGE WITH THE LADDER OF LIGHT: a forge sunk a full storey below a stone gallery that rings it on all sides, the gallery rail crossing the picture at uneven heights with bracket lanterns hung between, one great arched furnace mouth glowing in the pit wall at the far end, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre on the pit floor, a shaft of warm light falling from a crack high in the vault in flat stepped rungs of amber across the dais

TOWER FORGE WITH THE FIRE-MOSS: a tall narrow forge stacked up a stone chimney cut deep inside the mountain, one wide arched furnace mouth at the very bottom of the shaft breathing warm orange, a stair winding up one wall past landings set at uneven heights with iron brackets jutting between, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre at furnace level, a carpet of orange fire-moss spreading up the furnace wall and glowing brighter in chunky stepped patches wherever the heat presses hardest

TWIN-FURNACE HALL WITH THE STONE LANTERN ROW: a wide vaulted hall cut into the mountain's broad chest, two arched furnace mouths of plainly different sizes set side by side in the back wall with one breathing full orange and one banked to a deep red glow, heavy timber gantries crossing overhead at three uneven heights, a broad anvil on a stone dais between and forward of the two mouths set off-centre, a row of squat stone lanterns along the dais edge each cradling a coal that glows a different warm colour

CAVE FORGE BY THE POOL WITH THE SLOW LAVA FALL: a low rough cave forge beside a still hot pool cut into the mountain's base, stalactites of uneven length hanging from the irregular ceiling, a worn stone floor sloping toward the water, one wide arched furnace set into the back wall, a broad anvil on a stone dais pushed to one side, a thin fall of lava dropping from a crack in the vault into a stone bowl in slow flat orange bands

BELLOWS-HOUSE FORGE WITH THE ANVIL ROOTS: one wide arched furnace mouth breathing orange at the end of a broad timber-and-stone bellows hall inside the mountain, a broad anvil on an off-centre stone dais before it, a great timber wheel turning in a race of dark water set well to one side, three bellows of different sizes along the wall, iron roots growing from the anvil down into the dais stone and spreading in dark stepped lines across the floor

BRIDGE FORGE WITH THE FIRE FISH: a forge built on a broad stone bridge spanning a chasm inside the mountain, the drop glowing faintly on both sides, one arched furnace built into the bridge tower at the far end, a broad anvil on a dais set off-centre on the span, heavy stone parapets rising at uneven heights along each edge, a fish of living flame swimming lazy circles inside the furnace throat with chunky stepped fins catching the amber light

CALDERA LEDGE WORKSHOP WITH THE TUNING FORK: a wide stone workshop on a broad ledge inside the mountain's open crater, the glowing throat far below throwing warm light upward, a roof of timber and hide stretched over rough posts at uneven heights, one deep arched furnace set into the inner rock face, a broad anvil on a stone dais near the ledge's edge, a tuning fork as tall as the anvil standing upright on the dais and glowing in flat amber bands at its tips as it hums

CRYSTAL CAVERN FORGE WITH THE MOLTEN POOL MIRROR: a forge set among great amber crystal columns growing from floor to ceiling of a mountain cavern, each column throwing the fire back in chunky stepped facets, one arched furnace mouth cut between two columns at the far wall, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre among the columns, a round pool of molten metal in a stone basin beside the anvil holding a perfectly still reflection of the vault above

WATERFALL FORGE WITH THE EMBER BIRDS: a forge hall behind a curtain of falling water filling one whole side in flat pale bands, the arched furnace mouth set into the rock wall opposite breathing orange, steam rising in chunky billows where spray meets the heat, a broad anvil on a stone dais set to one side, heavy timber gantries crossing overhead at three uneven heights, a flock of tiny ember-birds rising from the furnace mouth and circling the gantries like sparks that have decided to fly

SUNKEN FORGE WITH THE SINGING ANVIL: a forge sunk a full storey below a stone gallery ringing it on all sides, the gallery rail crossing the picture at uneven heights with the heaviest bracket pushed well to one corner, the arched furnace set into the pit wall breathing deep orange, a broad anvil on a stone dais off-centre on the pit floor, rings of visible sound rippling outward from the anvil in flat amber bands as it hums warm and steady by itself

TERRACE FORGE WITH THE COAL GARDEN: a forge on the middle of three stone terraces stepping down the inside of the mountain, the terraces above and below lit by their own smaller fires at uneven heights, the arched furnace mouth set into the terrace wall behind breathing orange, a broad anvil on a stone dais near the terrace edge, a bed of coals beside the furnace laid out like a garden with small glowing flowers of slag growing from it in chunky stepped clusters

STAIR-WELL FORGE WITH THE EMBER HOURGLASS: a forge at the bottom of a deep round stair-well cut down through the mountain, a stair spiralling up the curved wall in uneven flights toward a bright opening far above, the arched furnace mouth set into the well wall breathing orange, a broad anvil on a stone dais off to one side of the floor, an hourglass as tall as the anvil standing beside the dais running with glowing embers instead of sand with chunky stepped sides catching the warm light

OPEN-SIDED FLANK FORGE WITH THE STONE ARM BELLOWS: a forge hall high on the volcano's shoulder open through three wide arches of unequal span to the bright open air, one great arched furnace set into the inner mountain wall breathing deep orange, heavy stone piers between the arches at uneven heights, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre beneath the narrowest arch, a carved stone arm set into the inner wall working a large bellows with slow deliberate strokes in flat amber light

OBSIDIAN HALL WITH THE SLEEPING SALAMANDER: a hall of black glassy volcanic stone whose chunky stepped sides throw the fire back in flat amber bands, a wide arched furnace low in the back wall, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre toward the right, heavy iron-banded timbers crossing overhead at three uneven heights, a fat orange salamander curled asleep in the coal bed with the flames licking warm around it

DOME FORGE WITH THE WHISPERING VENTS: a forge under a great domed chamber of fitted stone with a round opening at its crown letting a shaft of daylight down onto the floor, one arched furnace mouth low in the curved wall at the far end, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre beneath the shaft, a row of small stone vents in the curved wall breathing out slow curls of coloured steam in flat stepped bands of amber and green

CLIFF-MOUTH FORGE WITH THE STONE TORTOISE: a forge set in the mouth of a cave high on the outer cliff of the volcano with the sky and distant lowlands open and bright beyond the near edge, the arched furnace cut deep into the cave wall at the back, timber gantries crossing at uneven heights behind, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre toward the opening, a stone tortoise the size of the anvil carrying the water trough on its broad back beside the dais

GEYSER FORGE WITH THE WIND CHIMES OF IRON: a forge beside a geyser vent in the mountain floor throwing up a column of steam caught mid-rise in chunky stepped white, one great arched furnace mouth set into the wall behind glowing amber at its throat, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off to one side, heavy timber gantries crossing the vault at uneven heights, a cluster of iron chimes hung from the vault above turning slowly in the rising heat and ringing

TOWER FORGE WITH THE MIRROR SHIELD: a tall narrow forge stacked up a chimney of stone deep inside the mountain, the arched furnace mouth wide and low at the very bottom breathing orange across the floor, a stair winding up one wall past timber landings at uneven heights, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre at furnace level, a great polished round shield hung on the near wall throwing the furnace light back as a second fire across the stone

CAVE FORGE BY THE POOL WITH THE MOTH OF ASH: a low rough cave forge beside a still hot pool cut into the mountain's base, stalactites of uneven length hanging from the irregular ceiling, a worn stone floor sloping toward the water, one wide arched furnace set into the back wall, a broad anvil on a stone dais pushed to one side, a single great grey moth of ash resting open-winged on the furnace lintel with its wings edged in ember and chunky stepped markings of warm amber across every flight feather

LAVA-FED SMITHY WITH THE CHAIN OF TOOLS: a low stone smithy with one wide arched furnace mouth in its back wall, built over a bright molten channel running across its floor, a black stone bridge over it sitting off-centre, three stone sluice gates of different sizes along one edge with the smallest pulled well aside, a broad anvil on a stone dais beside the channel, tongs and hammers and files hanging by themselves in a slow-turning ring in the warm air above the dais catching the orange glow

ROOT-HALL FORGE WITH THE EMBER FOUNTAIN: a forge hall where the roots of a giant tree come down through the ceiling and grip the stone walls at uneven heights, one arched furnace mouth glowing orange between two great root-columns, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre toward the left wall, a stone fountain beside the dais throwing up a slow plume of embers instead of water, the embers falling back in chunky stepped arcs of amber and deep red around the dais

TWIN-FURNACE HALL WITH THE STONE FACE DOOR: a wide hall cut into the mountain's core with two arched furnace mouths of plainly different sizes side by side in the back wall, one breathing orange and one banked to a deep red glow, heavy timber gantries spanning the hall at three uneven heights, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre between and in front of the two mouths, a carved stone face filling the larger furnace mouth so its open jaw serves as the fire door

PILLARED UNDERCROFT WITH THE WHISPERING VENTS: a low forge in an undercroft of thick squat pillars marching away in uneven rows beneath the mountain's root, one arched furnace mouth glowing warm orange between two pillars at the back wall, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre in the near bay, a row of small stone vents low in the side wall breathing out slow curls of coloured steam in flat stepped bands of amber and pale green across the rough stone face

BELLOWS-HOUSE FORGE WITH THE RUNNER OF EMBERS: a broad timber-and-stone bellows hall cut inside the mountain, one wide arched furnace mouth breathing orange at its far end, a broad anvil on an off-centre stone dais set before it, a great timber wheel turning in a race of dark water well to one side, three bellows of different sizes ranged along the wall at uneven heights, a line of embers laid along the floor from the furnace mouth to the anvil glowing like a lit carpet of chunky stepped amber dots

OPEN-SIDED FLANK FORGE WITH THE SINGING ANVIL: a forge hall high on the volcano's shoulder opening through three wide arches of unequal span to the open air, one great arched furnace set into the inner mountain wall breathing orange, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre beneath the narrowest arch, heavy stone piers of different thicknesses dividing the open face, rings of visible sound rippling outward from the anvil in flat amber bands as it hums by itself in the warm light

TWIN-FURNACE HALL WITH THE HANGING BELL TREE: a wide vaulted hall cut into the mountain's core, two arched furnace mouths of plainly different sizes side by side in the back wall with one breathing orange and one banked to a deep red glow, a broad anvil on a stone dais between and in front of them set off-centre, heavy timber gantries crossing at three uneven heights overhead, a bare iron tree beside the larger furnace hung with dozens of small bells that stir and tilt in the rising heat

ROOT-HALL FORGE WITH THE LAMP-EYED OWL: a forge hall where the great roots of a giant tree come down through the ceiling and grip the rough stone walls in thick curving columns, one arched furnace mouth breathing orange between two root-columns at the back wall, a broad anvil on a stone dais set off-centre toward the right, timber gantries wedged between the roots at uneven heights, a stone owl perched on the nearest gantry with two round chunky eyes lit amber from within like lamps

CAVE FORGE BY THE POOL WITH THE FIRE-MOSS: a low rough cave forge cut into the mountain's base beside a still hot pool, stalactites of uneven length hanging from the irregular ceiling, a worn stone floor sloping gently toward the water's edge, one wide arched furnace set into the back wall breathing orange, a broad anvil on a stone dais pushed to one side, a carpet of orange fire-moss climbing the furnace wall in chunky stepped patches glowing brighter in flat amber bands wherever the heat presses close
